caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 247 of 1995 with Civil Rule No. 387 (FM) of 1995.
lawyer:
Joynal Abedin, Advocate -----For the Appellant. 
Md. Amirul Islam with Tania Amir, Advocates ----- For the Respondent No.1.
parties:
Sarhind Garments Ltd ----- Appellant
Vs
Glory Truth Industries Ltd and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal at the instance of the plaintiff appellant is directed against the Judgment and order dated 28-11-1995 passed by the 5th Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. in Title Suit No. 143 of 1995 refusing to grant an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendant respondent Nos. 1 and 2 from demanding payment and paying the amount as contemplated in the back to back LC No. 01-00281-95 dated 9-3-1995. 

 3. The defendant respondent No. 1 opened an irrevocable Master Letter of Credit (LC) FKB 950138 dated 14-2-95 through Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Ltd. Hong Kong in favour of the plaintiff for supply of 54,000 pieces of Men's 100% Cotton Woven Sports Shirt to Walmart Stores Inc. USA for US Dollar 358020.00. In terms of the said Master LC the plaintiff-appellant was required to make shipment of the said finished garments between 31st March and 15th April, 1995. The defendant respondent No. 1 opened the said Master LC in favour of the plaintiff-appellant on 14-2-1995 on condition that the plaintiff-appellant would buy fabrics and accessories from the defendant-respondent No. 1 by opening back to back LC and accordingly, the plaintiff-appellant on receipt of the said Master LC had drawn back to back LC. No. 01-00281-95 dated 9-3-1995 through their bank namely, National Bank Limited i.e. defendant-respondent No. 2 of the instant appeal for importing fabrics and accessories of US Dollar 2,47,316.48 equivalent to Taka 99,68,239.10 as per proforma Invoice Nos. P-032/94 P-038/94 and P-0041/94 of the defendant respondent No. 1. After the said back to back LC dated 9-3-1995 was opened by the plaintiff appellant in favour of the defendant-respondent No. 1 for supply of fabrics and accessories the defendant-respondent No. 1 over telephone and by a letter dated 10-3-1995 requested the plaintiff-appellant to take delivery of fabrics and accessories already sent by them on account of their party in Bangladesh under bill of lading dated 16-1-1995 by fraudulent representation that the said consignments of fabrics and accessories were in order and would conform to the contract specifications mentioned in the aforesaid back to back LC, knowing fully well that the said consignments were defective and accordingly, these were rejected by the third party. The plaintiff appellant relying on such assurances and representations agreed to take delivery of the same from the port by paying necessary customs and port duties. Since the said consignments of fabrics and accessories were sent to a third party by the defendant respondent No. 1 it took a long time for the plaintiff appellant to clear the said consignments from the port. The plaintiff appellant ultimately succeeded in taking delivery of the said consignments in the first part of April, 1995 and the plaintiff-appellant received the consignments at its factory premises on 12-4-1995. Before the said consignments were cleared from the port and received at the factory premises the defendant respondent No. 1 by fax dated 11-3-1995 gave an undertaking to the plaintiff appellant that if the said consignments of the fabrics and accessories were found to be bad or defective the defendant respondent No. 1 would remain responsible and liable for the same. The plaintiff-appellant immediately after arrival of the said consignments at the factory premises vide their letter dated 12-4-1995 informed the local agent of the defendant respondent No. 1 that inspection of the said consignments will be held immediately and requested their local agent namely, M/S Rasel International to send their representative at the time of inspection and the inspection of the said consignments was done on 14-4-1995 and it was found that the goods were defective because of colour shading, weaving defects in every yard of the fabric and also cut pieces and it is asserted that this inspection took place in presence of one Mr. Pooni who is said to be representative of Walmart in Bangladesh. The representative of M/S Rasel International was also present. After the said inspection the defendant respondent No. 1 was duly informed of the said defects in the fabrics both by the local agent of the defendant respondent No. 1 as well as the plaintiff appellant. The plaintiff appellant by a letter dated 18-4-1995 while informing about the defective fabrics also requested the defendant respondent No. 1 to accept the finished garments made with the defective fabrics by extending the period of shipment by amending the Master LC. The local agent of the defendant respondent No. 1 also assured the plaintiff appellant by fax dated 15-4-1995 and 11-5-1995 that the defendant-respondent No. 1 would arrange for resale of the said fabrics to some other party so that the plaintiff appellant do notsuffer any loss. Ultimately, they did nothing in that respect. The further case of the plaintiff appellant is that in this background of the matter, the plaintiff appellant carried out another inspection of the said fabrics by SGS (Bangladesh) Ltd. and obtained a report dated 4-7-1995 which also revealed that the said fabrics were defective because of the colour shading and cut pieces. The plaintiff appellant, therefore, by fax dated 4-7-95 informed the defendant respondent No. 1 about the said position and requested them to extend the period of shipment of the finished garments by making necessary amendments to the Master LC so that they could make finished garments and ship the same, but without any result. The plaintiff appellant by its letter dated 18-4-1995 also informed the National Bank Limited, that is the defendant respondent No. 2, about the said defect in the said fabrics and requested them to stop payment to the defendant respondent No. 1 under the said back to back LC dated 9-3-1995 because of the fraudulent representation made by the defendant respondent No. 1 regarding quality and contract specification of the said consignment. The due date of payment of the price of the said fabrics and accessories by the plaintiff appelIant to the defendant respondent No. 1 under the said back to back LC was 13-7-1995 but the defendant respondent No. 1 in spite of their promise and assurances to settle the matter, did not do so rather they took steps to receive payment of the full price of the said defective fabrics and accessories under the said back to back LC. In this background of the matter, the plaintiff appelIant was compelled to file the aforesaid Title Suit No. 143 of 1995 as well as an application for temporary injunction for restraining the defendant respondent Nos. 1 and 2 from taking and making payment of the price of the said defective fabrics and accessories under the back to back LC. After the defendant respondent No.1 received the summons from the Court of Subordinate Judge they duly appeared before him and prayed for time for filing written objection and the plaintiff appellant filed an application praying for ad interim injunction but the learned Subordinate Judge granted an order of status quo till the injunction matter is heard.
